summary: Removes the project-managed SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hook registrations from Codex/Claude/Gemini bootstrap while retaining zero-output compatibility stubs at the old script paths so already-running sessions with cached hook tables do not fail.
nonclaims: No user-level ~/.codex native oh-my-codex hook wrapper was rewritten.
Other project hooks such as Stop, PreToolUse, and PostToolUse remain registered.
The two legacy script paths remain as silent compatibility stubs only; bootstrap no longer registers them.

findings: Removed active context hook registrations instead of adding runtime flags; kept tiny compatibility stubs to avoid code-127 failures in already-running sessions.
Bootstrap-generated Codex, Claude, and Gemini hook surfaces now omit session/prompt context injection while retaining operational hooks.
A focused rg assertion fails if SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/BeforeAgent registrations reappear in managed configs/bootstrap, and the test asserts both legacy stubs emit zero bytes.
New sessions and prompt submissions no longer get repeated project-hook context blobs from managed hook registrations; existing sessions do not error if they cached the old script paths.
JSON configs parse; bash syntax checks pass; hook regression test passes; install dry-run verifies the 8 registered-hook script set and excludes context hooks.

alternatives: Remove all project-managed context hook entries and scripts
F6_alternatives.selected: Remove all project-managed context hook registrations and keep silent compatibility stubs for cached sessions.
rejected: Deleting scripts outright caused current cached UserPromptSubmit hooks to fail with code 127.
Removing only Codex would leave Claude/Gemini bootstrap surfaces able to reintroduce the same context blobs.

findings: Removing context-injection hooks reduces prompt-injection and accidental data-in-context surface.
Managed session/prompt startup no longer registers the two context hook scripts; cached sessions execute only zero-output stubs.
Canonical plain-git and contract-version doctrine remains in AGENTS/developer context; this change only removes noisy hook injection.
Reversal is a normal git revert; no live credential or cluster mutation was performed.
Config grep and JSON parsing provide direct evidence that the context hooks are no longer registered.
README and regression checks now distinguish active registered hooks from legacy no-op compatibility paths.

verification.evidence: all managed hook JSON files parse
compatibility stubs exit 0 and emit zero stdout/stderr
governance hook retired VCS surface tests passed
dry-run completed; hook scripts verified (8 scripts). Upstream agent-skills fetch warning was non-fatal and unrelated to hook registration removal.
